# medfit: Infrastructure for Mediation Analysis in R

[![CRAN
status](https://www.r-pkg.org/badges/version/medfit)](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=medfit)
[![Lifecycle:
stable](https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-stable-brightgreen.svg)](https://lifecycle.r-lib.org/articles/stages.html#stable)
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/Data-Wise/medfit/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Data-Wise/medfit/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![Codecov test
coverage](https://codecov.io/gh/Data-Wise/medfit/graph/badge.svg)](https://app.codecov.io/gh/Data-Wise/medfit)
[![pkgdown](https://github.com/Data-Wise/medfit/actions/workflows/pkgdown.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Data-Wise/medfit/actions/workflows/pkgdown.yaml)

**medfit** fits mediation models, pulls out the paths, and gives you
effects with intervals. One call to start; the same objects and
functions work for every model, from one mediator to a latent variable.

> **In one line:**
> [`med()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/med.md) runs a
> mediation analysis,
> [`quick()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/quick.md)
> prints it, and
> [`nie()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/nie.md),
> [`nde()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/nde.md),
> [`te()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/te.md),
> [`pm()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/pm.md) and
> [`tidy()`](https://generics.r-lib.org/reference/tidy.html) read it.

**Next:** [install](#install), then [run the
example](#start-here-in-60-seconds).

## Install

``` r

install.packages("medfit",
  repos = c("https://data-wise.r-universe.dev", "https://cloud.r-project.org"))
```

From GitHub instead: `pak::pak("data-wise/medfit")`. This installs the
version currently built by r-universe; check `packageVersion("medfit")`
afterward. Binaries exist for supported R and platform combinations; a
source installation can need a compiler for dependencies such as
`nloptr`.

> **CRAN has 0.3.2, which does not run the examples on this site.** It
> lacks `mediation_demo`,
> [`fit_sem()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/fit_sem.md),
> [`mbco_sem()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/mbco_sem.md)
> and the joint and cluster classes. Its two known issues, serial
> [`te()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/te.md)/[`pm()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/pm.md)
> and [`confint()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/confint.html) path rows, are
> fixed in 0.5.0; see
> [\#83](https://github.com/Data-Wise/medfit/issues/83).

## Start here in 60 seconds

`mediation_demo` ships with the package, so this runs as written:

``` r

library(medfit)

result <- med(
  data = mediation_demo,
  treatment = "treatment", mediator = "mediator1", outcome = "outcome",
  covariates = c("covariate1", "covariate2")
)
quick(result)
#> NIE = 0.333  | NDE = 0.206 | PM = 61.8 %
```

**You should see** one line. NIE is the indirect effect through the
mediator, NDE the direct effect, PM the share mediated. If you get an
error instead, see [When something fails](#when-something-fails).

**Then: read the pieces, get a table, add an interval**

``` r

nie(result)   # indirect effect (a * b)
nde(result)   # direct effect (c')
te(result)    # total effect
pm(result)    # proportion mediated
paths(result) # a, b, c'

library(generics)
tidy(result)   # every effect with its standard error
#> # A tibble: 6 × 3
#>   term    estimate std_error
#>   <chr>      <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 a          0.583    0.0989
#> 2 b          0.571    0.0535
#> 3 c_prime    0.206    0.110 
#> 4 nie        0.333    0.0645
#> 5 nde        0.206    0.110 
#> 6 te         0.539    0.119 

glance(result)  # one-row model summary
#> # A tibble: 1 × 6
#>     nie   nde    te    pm  nobs converged
#>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <int> <lgl>    
#> 1 0.333 0.206 0.539 0.618   400 TRUE     

# With a bootstrap interval
result_boot <- med(
  data = mediation_demo,
  treatment = "treatment", mediator = "mediator1", outcome = "outcome",
  covariates = c("covariate1", "covariate2"),
  boot = TRUE, n_boot = 1000, seed = 42
)
quick(result_boot)
#> NIE = 0.333  [0.208, 0.458] | NDE = 0.206 | PM = 61.8 %
```

## Pick your model

Find your data, open its page.

| I have | Start here |
|----|----|
| One mediator, a continuous outcome | [Simple mediation](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/articles/model-simple.html) |
| A binary or count variable | [Binary and non-normal variables](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/articles/model-glm-families.html) |
| Several mediators | [Parallel](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/articles/model-parallel.html), [serial](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/articles/model-serial.html) or [joint](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/articles/model-joint.html) mediation |
| Clusters (schools, clinics) or two-level data | [Cluster-randomized trials](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/articles/model-cluster.html), [two-level mediation](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/articles/model-twolevel.html) (experimental) |
| A lavaan fit, or a latent mediator | [lavaan fits](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/articles/model-lavaan.html), [the sem engine: a latent mediator](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/articles/model-sem-latent.html) |
| Missing data | [Bounded FIML](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/articles/model-fiml.html): numerically verified against lavaan, not statistically admitted (no interval coverage is established) |

Other cases (interaction, weights, constraints and MBCO, serial or
parallel models written as syntax) are on the [full Models
table](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/articles/models.html). Not
sure which engine? See [Which engine should I
use?](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/articles/guide-engines.html)

## More, when you need it

**What’s new in 0.21.2**

- **0.21.2 (2026-11-26, GitHub; CRAN submission is the maintainer’s):**
  no change to what any function returns; fixes the notes CRAN’s
  incoming checks raised (Rd usage, check time) and the open S7 issue on
  0.3.2, and moves the slowest tests and gates to the local full run.

- **0.21.1 (2026-11-26, GitHub only):** no change to the package code
  since 0.21.0 (released 2026-11-25); the longest test files are skipped
  on CRAN, the test warnings are gone, and the cookbook has recipe 25
  (MLR). The highlights of 0.21.0 follow.

- **0.21.0 (2026-11-25, GitHub only):** adds the MLR estimator and
  classed product refusals below since 0.20.0 (released 2026-11-23).

- **MLR estimator (0.21.0):** `fit_sem(model, data, estimator = "MLR")`
  keeps the ML estimates, uses sandwich standard errors and adds the
  Yuan-Bentler scaled chi-square (`chisq_scaled`, `scaling_factor`,
  `p_value_scaled` in
  [`glance()`](https://generics.r-lib.org/reference/glance.html)), as
  lavaan’s MLR. It is defined for single-level complete-data fits with
  linear equality constraints; anything else stops with a classed error.
  See the [NEWS](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/news/index.html).

- **Classed product refusals (0.21.0):** every refusal of the `:`
  product term has a class (`medfit_error_product_*`); messages and
  numbers are unchanged.

- **0.20.0 (2026-11-23, GitHub only):** adds the native two-level route
  below since 0.19.0 (released 2026-11-17). The two-level API is
  experimental, so it may change without a deprecation period.

- **Native two-level fit (0.20.0, experimental):**
  `fit_sem(model, data, cluster = )` fits a two-level (1-1-1) model
  written in `level:` blocks with the sem engine, and
  [`extract_mediation()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/extract_mediation.md)
  on the fit returns `TwoLevelMediationData`;
  `fit_mediation(engine = "sem", model = , cluster = )` returns the same
  object. `se_type = "sandwich"` gives cluster-robust standard errors.
  See the [model
  page](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/articles/model-twolevel.html).

- **Tests on native two-level fits (0.20.0, experimental):**
  [`mbco_sem()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/mbco_sem.md)
  tests the indirect effect at one level, and
  [`twolevel_equal_indirect()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/twolevel_equal_indirect.md)
  tests that the within and between indirect effects are equal; a
  pair-sign twin certificate stops a worse local optimum from standing
  in the equality refit.

- **Behavior change (0.20.0, experimental):** the within-only rule for a
  two-level fit now reads the unrestricted (h1) ICC on both routes, so
  within-only results are rarer. See the
  [NEWS](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/news/index.html).

- **Two-level parallel mediation (0.19.0, experimental):**
  [`extract_mediation()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/extract_mediation.md)
  on a two-level `lavaan` fit with two or more mediators returns
  `TwoLevelParallelMediationData`, with per-mediator and total effects
  at each level, delta-method SEs and
  [`twolevel_statistic()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/twolevel_statistic.md)
  for the bootstrap. One-mediator results are unchanged. See the [model
  page](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/articles/model-twolevel.html#several-parallel-mediators).

- **The sem engine (0.18.0):** `fit_mediation(engine = "sem")` names
  medfit’s own SEM fitter; `engine = "native"` still works, with
  identical results.
  [`sem_control()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/sem_control.md)
  collects its optimizer settings. See [Which engine should I
  use?](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/articles/guide-engines.html).

- **Renamed pages (0.18.0):** the sem engine articles moved
  (`native-guide` is now `sem-guide`, and so on); old links redirect.

- **Bounded FIML expansion (0.17.0):** one or two covariates, two
  parallel and two serial mediators (numerically verified, not
  statistically admitted). See the [model
  page](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/articles/model-fiml.html).

- **Two-level mediation (0.17.0, experimental):**
  [`extract_mediation()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/extract_mediation.md)
  on a two-level `lavaan` fit returns `TwoLevelMediationData`; lavaan
  floor 0.7-3. See the [model
  page](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/articles/model-twolevel.html).

- **Before that:** 0.16.0 (both sign branches of a nonzero-product
  equality, corrected constrained standard errors) and 0.15.0 (native
  defaults flip: `fixed_x` and `meanstructure` on when unset).

Every release is listed in
[NEWS](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/news/index.html); upgrading
from CRAN 0.3.2? See [What changed since CRAN
0.3.2](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/articles/guide-changes.html).

**Bounded FIML (0.16.0 and 0.17.0): settings and limits**

medfit 0.16.0 added explicit
`fit_sem(missing = "fiml", fixed_x = FALSE)` for three-variable Gaussian
random-X mediation, preserving listwise defaults. medfit 0.17.0 also
fits one or two covariates, two parallel mediators (with zero, one or
two covariates) and two-mediator serial models (the saturated graph or
the pure chain, with up to two covariates; implemented and verified
against lavaan, not calibrated for coverage). It is unavailable in
0.15.0 and earlier. Observed/model SEs and unstandardized effects and
normal intervals are supported. The model requires continuous X, M and
Y, a free or exactly zero direct path, independent Gaussian
disturbances, free intercepts and ignorable missingness under that joint
model. Native
[`fit_mediation()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/fit_mediation.md)
uses `engine_args` for the same opt-in. Extracted FIML objects refuse
[`quick()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/quick.md),
[`pm()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/pm.md) and
[`glance()`](https://generics.r-lib.org/reference/glance.html); fit
tests, profiles and MBCO remain unavailable. Source-fit retained-row and
Gaussian parameter-draw intervals
(`bootstrap_mediation(source_fit = ...)`) are implemented but withheld:
the call is refused until statistical admission is decided.
[`glance()`](https://generics.r-lib.org/reference/glance.html) on the
source SEMFit retains likelihood/IC fields. See the [native
guide](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/articles/sem-guide.html#bounded-fiml)
for settings and limits.

**Already have fitted models?** (`lm`, `glm`, `lmer`, lavaan)

[`extract_mediation()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/extract_mediation.md)
turns fitted models into the same objects (see [Model
Extraction](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/articles/extraction.html)):

``` r

fit_m <- lm(mediator1 ~ treatment + covariate1 + covariate2, data = mediation_demo)
fit_y <- lm(outcome ~ treatment + mediator1 + covariate1 + covariate2, data = mediation_demo)
med_data <- extract_mediation(fit_m, model_y = fit_y, treatment = "treatment", mediator = "mediator1")
nie(med_data)
```

**Cluster-randomized trial** (treatment assigned to schools, clinics)

When the treatment is assigned to whole clusters (such as schools), use
the `lmer` engine (needs the suggested `lme4`; add `se_type = "kr"` with
`pbkrtest` for few clusters):

``` r

# 40 schools of 10 students, treatment assigned by school
set.seed(123)
J <- 40
n <- 10
school <- rep(seq_len(J), each = n)
cdat <- data.frame(school = factor(school), X = sample(rep(0:1, J / 2))[school])
cdat$M <- 0.5 * cdat$X + rnorm(J, sd = 0.5)[school] + rnorm(J * n)
cdat$Y <- 0.2 * cdat$X + 0.4 * cdat$M + rnorm(J, sd = 0.5)[school] + rnorm(J * n)

fit <- fit_mediation(
  Y ~ X + M, M ~ X, data = cdat,
  treatment = "X", mediator = "M",
  engine = "lmer", cluster = "school"
)

nie(fit)        # a * b_between
decompose(fit)  # own-mediator and spillover parts (large-cluster approximation)
```

    #> Natural Indirect Effect (NIE): 0.328
    #>        own  spillover        nie
    #> 0.25763321 0.07036432 0.32799753

See [Methods and
Formulas](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/articles/methods.html) for
the estimand and the assumptions each effect needs.

**Latent mediator** (sem engine)

When the mediator is a construct measured by several indicators, write
the model as syntax. The sem engine needs no other package:

``` r

# a latent mediator `eta` with three indicators, simulated
set.seed(11)
n <- 400
X <- rnorm(n)
eta <- 0.5 * X + rnorm(n, sd = 0.9)
ldat <- data.frame(
  X = X,
  m1 = eta + rnorm(n, sd = 0.7),
  m2 = 0.8 * eta + rnorm(n, sd = 0.7),
  m3 = 0.7 * eta + rnorm(n, sd = 0.8)
)
ldat$Y <- 0.4 * eta + 0.2 * X + rnorm(n, sd = 0.8)

syntax <- "
  eta =~ m1 + m2 + m3
  eta ~ a * X
  Y ~ b * eta + cp * X
"
fit <- fit_mediation(model = syntax, data = ldat, treatment = "X",
                     mediator = "eta", engine = "sem")
nie(fit)

mbco_sem(fit_sem(syntax, ldat), "a", "b")  # minimum of two likelihood-ratio tests
```

    #> Natural Indirect Effect (NIE): 0.1685
    #>
    #>  Minimum-of-two likelihood-ratio tests (MBCO) for an indirect effect
    #>
    #> data:  a * b = 0
    #> MBCO = 46.753, df = 1, p-value = 8.054e-12

**Classes and functions**

| Class | Models |
|----|----|
| `MediationData` | Simple mediation: X to M to Y (paths a, b, c’) |
| `InteractionMediationData` | Treatment-by-mediator interaction, four-way decomposition (CDE, INTref, INTmed, PIE) |
| `SerialMediationData` | A chain X to M1 to M2 to Y; [`nie()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/nie.md) is the chain, [`te()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/te.md)/[`pm()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/pm.md) count every path |
| `ParallelMediationData` | Mediators side by side; indirect effect is the sum of a_j \* b_j |
| `JointMediationData` | Joint natural effects of several mediators with products |
| `ClusterMediationData` | Treatment assigned to clusters (2-1-1): own-mediator and spillover parts |
| `TwoLevelMediationData` | A two-level `lavaan` fit with X, M and Y on level-1 units (1-1-1): the indirect effect at the within and the between level (0.17.0, experimental) |
| `TwoLevelParallelMediationData` | The same two-level fit with two or more parallel mediators: per-mediator and total effects at each level (0.19.0, experimental) |
| `FIMLMediationData`, `FIMLParallelMediationData`, `FIMLSerialMediationData` | Bounded FIML fits (`fit_sem(missing = "fiml")`): X to M to Y, two parallel mediators, two serial mediators (see above) |
| `SEMFit` | A sem engine fit; [`extract_mediation()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/extract_mediation.md) turns it into the classes above |
| `BootstrapResult` | Point estimates, intervals and the bootstrap distribution |

| You want to | Call |
|----|----|
| Run a mediation in one step | [`med()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/med.md), [`quick()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/quick.md) |
| Read effects and paths | [`nie()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/nie.md), [`nde()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/nde.md), [`te()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/te.md), [`pm()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/pm.md), [`paths()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/paths.md), [`decompose()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/decompose.md) |
| Get a table | [`tidy()`](https://generics.r-lib.org/reference/tidy.html), [`glance()`](https://generics.r-lib.org/reference/glance.html), [`confint()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/confint.html), [`coef()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/coef.html), [`vcov()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/vcov.html), [`nobs()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/nobs.html) |
| Fit with control | [`fit_mediation()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/fit_mediation.md) (engines `glm`, `regmedint`, `lmer`, `sem`) |
| Use fitted models | [`extract_mediation()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/extract_mediation.md) (lm, glm, lmer, lavaan, `SEMFit`) |
| Write a model as syntax | [`fit_sem()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/fit_sem.md), [`mbco_sem()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/mbco_sem.md) |
| Bootstrap | [`bootstrap_mediation()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/bootstrap_mediation.md) (parametric, nonparametric, plugin) |

Every function is on the [Reference
Card](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/articles/refcard.html). For the
classes, see the
[Introduction](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/articles/introduction.html);
for resampling, [Bootstrap
Inference](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/articles/bootstrap.html).

**Mediationverse ecosystem and related packages**

medfit is the foundation for the **mediationverse** ecosystem:

| Package | Purpose | Role |
|----|----|----|
| **medfit** (this) | Model fitting, extraction, bootstrap | Foundation |
| [RMediation](https://github.com/data-wise/rmediation) | Confidence intervals (DOP, MBCO) | Application |
| [probmed](https://github.com/data-wise/probmed) | Probabilistic effect size (P_med) | Application |
| [medrobust](https://github.com/data-wise/medrobust) | Sensitivity analysis | Application (independent of medfit) |
| [medsim](https://github.com/data-wise/medsim) | Simulation infrastructure | Support |
| [mediationverse](https://github.com/data-wise/mediationverse) | Meta-package | Ecosystem |

See [Ecosystem
Coordination](https://github.com/Data-Wise/mediation-planning/blob/main/docs/ECOSYSTEM-COORDINATION.md)
for version compatibility and development guidelines.

Also: [Package documentation](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/),
[Development
Guide](https://github.com/data-wise/medfit/blob/main/CLAUDE.md),
[NEWS](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/news/index.html).

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Development status

CRAN has an older release (0.3.2), and this site documents the GitHub
build (see the callout under Install). Current development adds
mediation structures and inference on the `dev` branch; see `NEWS.md`
for what each release contains.

### Code quality

- **Defensive Programming**: checkmate for input validation, S7
  validators for class integrity
- **Testing**: 2,600+ `test_that()` blocks (\>90% coverage, enforced via
  codecov)
- **CI/CD**: R CMD check, lintr, coverage reporting via GitHub Actions

See the [NEWS](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/news/index.html) for
what changed in each release.

## Contributing

This package is in active development. Contributions are welcome!
Please:

1.  Fork the repository
2.  Create a feature branch from `dev`
3.  Make your changes with tests
4.  Submit a pull request to `dev`

# Package index

## Quick Start

Short entry points for rapid analysis

- [`med()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/med.md) :
  Simple Mediation Analysis
- [`quick()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/quick.md) :
  Quick Summary of Mediation Results

## Data

Simulated example data

- [`mediation_demo`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/mediation_demo.md)
  : Simulated Mediation Data for Examples

## Effect Extractors

Extract mediation effects from fitted models

- [`nie()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/nie.md) :
  Extract Natural Indirect Effect (NIE)
- [`nde()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/nde.md) :
  Extract Natural Direct Effect (NDE)
- [`te()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/te.md) : Extract
  Total Effect (TE)
- [`pm()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/pm.md) : Extract
  Proportion Mediated (PM)
- [`paths()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/paths.md) :
  Extract All Path Coefficients
- [`decompose()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/decompose.md)
  : Decomposition of a Mediation Effect
- [`joint_effects()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/joint_effects.md)
  : Joint Effects at a Given Parameter Vector

## S7 Classes

Core S7 class definitions for mediation data structures

- [`MediationData()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/MediationData.md)
  : MediationData S7 Class
- [`SerialMediationData()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/SerialMediationData.md)
  : SerialMediationData S7 Class
- [`ParallelMediationData()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/ParallelMediationData.md)
  : ParallelMediationData: Parallel (Multiple-Mediator) Mediation
  Structure
- [`InteractionMediationData()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/InteractionMediationData.md)
  : InteractionMediationData: Mediation with Treatment-Mediator
  Interaction
- [`JointMediationData()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/JointMediationData.md)
  : JointMediationData: Joint Natural Effects of Multiple Mediators
- [`ClusterMediationData()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/ClusterMediationData.md)
  : ClusterMediationData: Cluster-Level Treatment Mediation (2-1-1)
- [`TwoLevelMediationData()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/TwoLevelMediationData.md)
  : TwoLevelMediationData Class
- [`TwoLevelParallelMediationData()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/TwoLevelParallelMediationData.md)
  : TwoLevelParallelMediationData Class
- [`BootstrapResult()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/BootstrapResult.md)
  : BootstrapResult S7 Class
- [`SEMFit()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/SEMFit.md) :
  SEMFit S7 Class

## Model Fitting

Functions for fitting and extracting mediation models

- [`extract_mediation()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/extract_mediation.md)
  : Extract Mediation Structure from Fitted Models
- [`fit_mediation()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/fit_mediation.md)
  : Fit Mediation Models
- [`fit_sem()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/fit_sem.md)
  : Fit a Structural Equation Model by Maximum Likelihood
- [`mbco_sem()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/mbco_sem.md)
  : Minimum-of-k Likelihood-Ratio Test for an Indirect Effect (MBCO)
- [`sem_control()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/sem_control.md)
  : Optimizer settings for the sem engine
- [`compare_lr()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/compare_lr.md)
  : Compare medfit's Product-Null LR with OpenMx or lavaan
- [`medfit-syntax`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/medfit-syntax.md)
  [`medfit_syntax`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/medfit-syntax.md)
  : medfit Model Syntax
- [`bootstrap_mediation()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/bootstrap_mediation.md)
  : Perform Bootstrap Inference for Mediation Statistics
- [`twolevel_statistic()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/twolevel_statistic.md)
  : Bootstrap Callback for Two-Level Mediation
- [`twolevel_equal_indirect()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/twolevel_equal_indirect.md)
  **\[experimental\]** : Test equal indirect effects across the two
  levels of a native two-level fit

## Methods

tidy() and glance() for medfit classes; print, summary, anova, confint
and logLik methods for SEMFit

- [`tidy_s7_object()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/tidy_s7_object.md)
  [`glance_s7_object()`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/tidy_s7_object.md)
  : Tidy, Glance, and Inference Methods for medfit Objects
- [`SEMFit-methods`](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/reference/SEMFit-methods.md)
  : Methods for SEMFit objects
